about: Read by scripts/test.mjs (scripts/lib/suite-run.mjs). floors: the fewest tests a file may report (# tests N); a floor is a minimum, lower it only when tests are removed on purpose. names: the top-level test names a file must report (the census and the secret scanners); print a file's names with `node scripts/test.mjs --names <file>`. Every file of the roster has exactly one entry.

scripts/lib/git-env-census.test.mjs: census: a git spawn whose env is built by gitEnv() is clean and is counted
census: a git spawn with NO env: key is a finding naming file:line
census: env: process.env is REFUSED -- presence of an env: key is not safety
census: a spread of process.env is refused, including when gitEnv() is ALSO present (ordering re-adds GIT_*)
census: an env that is not produced by gitEnv() is refused; an alias assigned from gitEnv() in the same file is accepted
census: a multi-line call is read whole; the finding names the line the call STARTS on
census: a call inside a // or * comment line is ignored; a URL string earlier on the SAME line does not hide a real call
census: every spawn form is covered -- execFile, spawn, execSync/exec with a git command string, the qualified child_process form

census: a spawn whose command is neither a literal nor process.execPath cannot be proven not-git and is refused
census: an unreadable file (text null) is a finding, never a silent zero
census: findings are reported per file across a map, in walk order
census: a file that never binds child_process is skipped whole -- prose that looks like a call is not one
census: an aliased import (as) is followed to the real function, so an alias cannot hide a spawn

scripts/secret-scan.test.mjs: every named pattern fires on its own runtime-assembled sample, and names only itself
prose that names a prefix is not a hit
the generic rule: a high-entropy value assigned to a key-like name fires
the generic rule cannot fire on hashes, SHAs, UUIDs, references or low-entropy values
a .NET ResX file reference: the closing </value> tag is not part of the public key token before it
a long identifier on the right of a secret-named left side is code, not a literal
a real machine-generated secret on an edge of the code-value guard still fires
an environment-variable NAME held by a constant named for it is not a secret
the pointer-name quiet case is narrow: a plain secret name, or a real secret on a pointer name, still fires
a stateless installation token is a github-token wherever it sits, and the legacy 40-character form still is
a ghs_ mention that is not a stateless token is not a hit
a stateless installation token fires whatever its first segment is, digits or not, even absent
a short stateless installation token, about 120 characters after the prefix, still fires
a ghs_ body of 99 characters is not a hit, and one of exactly 100 is: the floor is pinned from both sides
a decoy that fails a pattern check cannot hide a real value later on the same line
two values of one pattern on one line are two hits with two fingerprints
a pattern hit does not suppress a generic hit on the same line, and two generic values are two hits
a skipped reference cannot swallow a real value joined to it by "&" (a query string)
a value a pattern already matched is not reported a second time by the generic rule
a hit carries line, pattern and fingerprint — never the value
a fingerprint is stable per file, pattern and value, and differs across files
scanPatch scans ADDED lines only, with new-file line numbers, including a "++" content line
parsePushRefs reads git lines and REFUSES a malformed one
rangeArgs: deletion skips, new branch and unknown remote scan against all remotes, else remote..local
a 200k-character line dense with key-like names scans in linear work (no catastrophic backtracking)
scanPatch unquotes every C escape git uses in a name, so a quoted name fingerprints like the tree
an assignment written "=>" (PHP) or ":=" (Go) is read as an assignment
a provider key right after a literal backslash-n/r/t or a %XX escape is still a key
a GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE a hook inherited are dropped: every fixture git call acts on its own repository
sameDir: a directory is itself however it is spelled, two directories are never one, and a path that does not resolve fails closed
sameDir: a link and its target are one directory, though their paths differ, and git's answer from inside the link is that directory (the macOS leg)
a repository reached by its 8.3 short name is the directory git reports: real paths are compared, not spellings (the Windows runner)
a fixture call is handed GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and no other GIT_ name beyond the three the flock allows, whatever the process inherited
the fixtures run in the test's own sandbox: a hostile global git config and HOME never reach them, and the fixture folders live inside it
the pushed range scans a file git calls binary (a NUL byte, a -diff attribute), unless the caller skips its path
a key in a pushed commit message or annotated-tag message is a hit, never the value
with the push remote named, only THAT remote's tracking refs count as already pushed
every pushed hit names the ref it was found under, once per ref, so acknowledgments can be read per ref
a key-like token deep inside a long snake_case name is found, before or after it
a pushed ref whose object is not a commit (a tag of a blob or a tree) is refused, never passed
a non-secret assignment cannot swallow the secret assignment in its own value
a key in an INNER annotated tag of a tag chain is a hit naming that tag object, never the value
a three-deep tag chain is walked to the bottom, and a key in the OUTER message is still a hit
a tag chain longer than the bound FAILS CLOSED instead of passing partly read
a tag object that points back at one already read FAILS CLOSED on the repeat itself, not on the depth bound
a tag object missing the object header, the type header, or both FAILS CLOSED with ETAGCHAIN
